newsitem.title: UK: ROWING-HENLEY NEEDS TO ATTRACT MORE INTERNATIONALS.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-HENLEY NEEDS TO ATTRACT MORE INTERNATIONALS.

text.p: The Henley Royal Regatta, known as much for its place in the British social calendar as the sporting agenda, was criticised by a top British official on Friday.

David Tanner, international manager of the Amateur Rowing Association (ARA) and British Olympic rowing team manager since 1991, said Henley needed to move forward with the times by attracting more high quality international crews.

On the third day of this annual five-day event, Tanner said Henley needed to "move up a gear" by putting in more funding and even offering prize money to attract a higher calibre and number of international crews to ensure its place as an important showcase for international talent.
Some of the top level events have as few as two or three entries and Tanner said he would like to see this climb to at least seven or eight.

"Henley in a narrow sense is not important in the rowing world because we do not have enough international level crews racing. But in a broader sense it is extremely important because it shows rowing can work as a sport," he said.
"Henley is a great event because it encourages people to come even if it is for the social side, but it is also run as a very good business and broadens the appeal of the sport."
Henley does attract crews from abroad, with 86 overseas entries this year, but over a third of these are from the United States and most are club crews rather than internationals.
"Henley is a U.S. tradition, not a European one and we need to have a breakthrough there if we are to see a truly international level of competition," Tanner said.
Around 18 foreign crews have moved through to Saturday's races with two more yet to race.
On Friday's third day of five, Britain's Guin Batten and Sweden's Maria Brandin glide comfortably through to Saturday's semifinals of the women's sculls event, the Princess Royal Cup.

In the men's sculling event, the Diamond Sculls, British international Greg Searle will meet U.S. international Jamie Koven in the semifinals while former British lightweight world champion Peter Haining faces Matthijs Van der Schoot of The Netherlands.
